name: Event Log Transformations
description: Compares two object-centric event logs. Reports strict equality across every relation, structural equivalence up to identifier and generated-type renaming (a bounded color-refinement bijection), reciprocal coverage percentages when they differ, and suspected automatic renames (case, whitespace or normalization differences — e.g. a SQLite export sanitizing a table name) on object-type, event-type and attribute names. The structural check is an explicitly bounded approximation, not a full graph-isomorphism decision.

maxEntities.title: Max entities per log
maxEntities.description: Safety cap on events + objects pulled into memory for the structural check. Beyond this the structural verdict is reported as undetermined rather than guessed.

maxSearchNodes.title: Isomorphism search budget
maxSearchNodes.description: Backtracking nodes explored when color refinement leaves a renaming ambiguous (the logs have non-trivial automorphisms). 0 disables the search — color-histogram evidence only.

renameSimilarity.title: Suspected-rename threshold
renameSimilarity.description: Jaro–Winkler similarity above which two otherwise-unmatched names are flagged as a likely automatic rename.

typeNamesOpaque.title: Treat type names as renameable
typeNamesOpaque.description: Exclude object-type and event-type names from the structural signature, so an automatic rename does not by itself count as a structural difference.

authors.name: István Koren
authors.affiliation: ELTE University Budapest, Data Science and Engineering

citation.text: Strict equality and structural isomorphism follow the OCEL equivalence definitions of the transformation-calculus draft (Definitions 1–2). The structural decision procedure is a bounded 1-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman color refinement with a capped backtracking search, not a complete isomorphism test.

author: István Koren
